alt.en: A printed page of music, page 8, headed "L'écho des montagnes de Béthléem, Noël languedocien", "No. 3" and "Musique de W. M.". Two upper voices sing "Les Anges, dans nos campagnes" while the bass staff rests, then all three voices sing "Glo-ri-a in excelsis Deo", with a part for piano or organ under each system.
alt.es: Página impresa de música, página 8, con el encabezado "L'écho des montagnes de Béthléem, Noël languedocien", "No. 3" y "Musique de W. M.". Dos voces agudas cantan "Les Anges, dans nos campagnes" mientras el pentagrama del bajo calla, y luego las tres voces cantan "Glo-ri-a in excelsis Deo", con una parte para piano u órgano bajo cada sistema.

caption.en: Les Anges, dans nos campagnes as No. 3 of Louis Lambillotte's Choix de cantiques sur des airs nouveaux, in its Paris edition of 1867; the book's 1842 edition holds the tune's earliest known printing, credited to "W. M."
caption.es: Les Anges, dans nos campagnes como n.º 3 del Choix de cantiques sur des airs nouveaux de Louis Lambillotte, en su edición de París de 1867; la edición de 1842 del libro contiene la primera impresión conocida de la melodía, atribuida a "W. M."

source: Choix de cantiques sur des airs nouveaux pour toutes les fêtes de l'année ... à trois ou quatre voix avec accompagnement d'orgue ou de piano par le R. P. L. Lambillotte (Paris: Poussielgue Frères, 1867), No. 3, "L'écho des montagnes de Béthléem", p. 8
library: Sibley Music Library, Eastman School of Music, University of Rochester
licenceEvidence: Library's item page: rights statement https://rightsstatements.org/page/NoC-US/1.0/ ("believes that the Item is in the Public Domain under the laws of the United States"). Printed Paris 1867; Lambillotte died 1855; the tune's "W. M." is unidentified, first published 1842: public domain by age everywhere (see rights.md).
credit: Sibley Music Library, Eastman School of Music, University of Rochester

alt.en: Part of a printed page of music headed "II. Our Blessed Lord. The Sacred Infancy." and "9. Christmas Hymn.", marked "Solo" and "Moderately": a single melody line in common time with one flat, with the words "The Angels we have heard on high, Most sweetly singing o'er our plains, And still the mountains in reply Are echoing their joyous strains" under the notes.
alt.es: Parte de una página impresa de música con los encabezados "II. Our Blessed Lord. The Sacred Infancy." y "9. Christmas Hymn.", marcada "Solo" y "Moderately": una sola línea de melodía en compasillo con un bemol, con la letra "The Angels we have heard on high, Most sweetly singing o'er our plains, And still the mountains in reply Are echoing their joyous strains" bajo las notas.

caption.en: James Chadwick's English, "The Angels we have heard on high", set to the French tune in the music book for The Holy Family Hymns (London, 1860), with a pickup note for the extra syllable at the start of each line.
caption.es: La versión inglesa de James Chadwick, "The Angels we have heard on high", con la melodía francesa en el libro de música de The Holy Family Hymns (Londres, 1860), con una nota de anacrusa para la sílaba de más al principio de cada verso.

source: Music for the Holy Family Hymns (London, Dublin and Derby: Richardson and Son, 1860), bound with The Holy Family Hymns (1860), p. 8, No. 9, "Christmas Hymn" (image n221)
library: Bodleian Library, University of Oxford (digitized by Google), via the Internet Archive
callNumber: Bodleian 147 d.193; Internet Archive TheHolyFamilyHymns1860; OCLC 607066425
licenceEvidence: Internet Archive record marks the item Public Domain Mark 1.0 (licenseurl http://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Published London 1860; Chadwick died 1882; the tune is anonymous ("W. M.", Paris 1842). Faithful scan of a flat page (see rights.md).
credit: Bodleian Library, University of Oxford, digitized by Google, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A printed page of four-part music on two staves, headed "Carol 181. Angels we have heard. (Christmas.) Old French Carol.", with the first verse under the notes, a long run of quick notes on "Glo" marked "Unison. ad lib.", and verses 2, 3 and 4 printed below, each ending "Gloria in excelsis Deo."
alt.es: Página impresa de música a cuatro voces en dos pentagramas, con el encabezado "Carol 181. Angels we have heard. (Christmas.) Old French Carol.", la primera estrofa bajo las notas, una larga carrera de notas rápidas sobre "Glo" marcada "Unison. ad lib." y las estrofas 2, 3 y 4 impresas debajo, cada una terminada en "Gloria in excelsis Deo."

caption.en: Carol 181 in Charles L. Hutchins's Carols Old and Carols New (Boston, 1916), the page our arrangement reads its tune and words from, in the four-part setting he had printed in his Boston weekly The Parish Choir in 1891.
caption.es: El villancico 181 de Carols Old and Carols New, de Charles L. Hutchins (Boston, 1916), la página de la que nuestro arreglo toma la melodía y la letra, en el arreglo a cuatro voces que él había impreso en su semanario de Boston The Parish Choir en 1891.

source: Carols Old and Carols New, for Use at Christmas and Other Seasons of the Christian Year, edited by Charles L. Hutchins (Boston: The Parish Choir, 1916), p. 157, Carol 181, "Angels we have heard", Old French Carol (image n182)
library: Princeton Theological Seminary Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Published Boston 1916 (the 1891 setting "Copyright, 1891, by C. L. Hutchins"); Hutchins died 1920; tune anonymous. US: published before 1931; EU and Israel: life plus 70 ended 1990. Faithful scan of a flat page (see rights.md).
